purpose: Per CEO R287 P2: 'Add the latest 2026 prior-art landscape to the TTP. Explicitly disclose that current technology already covers: physiologic sensor-driven valve actuation, obstruction detection, pressure-based closed-loop control, sensor-failure fallback, programmable/flow-regulated valves.'
constitutional_basis: Article X (honest disclosure). Article XXVIII (no silent semantic promotion — must disclose what is NOT novel).
honest_disclosure: The technical territory around 'sensor + controller + shunt valve + closed-loop control' is already very active. P-01's value proposition is NOT 'we invented closed-loop shunt control.' It is: 'Does bounded conductance-rate control produce a new robustness envelope under realistic sensor uncertainty?'

prior_art_landscape.title: Method and System to Control a Hydrocephalus Shunt System
what_it_does_NOT_cover: Bounded rate of conductance change (rate limiting)
Sensor-health-aware safe fallback (freeze on sensor failure)
Multi-segment parallel drainage with continuous redistribution
prior_art_landscape.relevance_to_P-01: This is the strongest existing closed-loop shunt patent. P-01's V2.1 controller (Arm D in our comparison) reproduces this approach as the incumbent baseline. P-01 V2.1 outperforms this approach by 2-3x in our computational testing.

prior_art_landscape.title: Methods and systems for treating hydrocephalus
what_it_covers: Controller-actuated valve using internal physiologic sensors
Keeping valve open using most recent valid sensor state when unsafe condition occurs
what_it_does_NOT_cover: Bounded rate of conductance change (explicit rate limiting at 2%/sec)
Multi-segment parallel drainage with continuous redistribution (not isolation)
prior_art_landscape.relevance_to_P-01: CRITICAL. This 2026 patent explicitly covers sensor failure handling and fallback — including 'keeping the valve open using the most recent valid sensor state.' This is very close to P-01's sensor-health fallback. The buyer's IP counsel MUST assess whether P-01's specific implementation (freeze alpha + bounded rate + multi-segment redistribution) is novel over this patent. P-01's differentiation may be NARROWER than previously thought.
prior_art_landscape.honest_assessment: This patent significantly raises the novelty bar for P-01. The sensor-health fallback concept is now in the published prior art. P-01's remaining differentiation is: (1) bounded RATE of conductance change (not just fallback), (2) multi-segment continuous redistribution (not single-valve), (3) the specific combination producing measurable robustness advantage. These are narrow differentiators.

prior_art_landscape.title: Implantable fluid pressure and flow sensor with drift compensation
prior_art_landscape.relevance_to_P-01: This patent covers sensor drift compensation and ML-based valve adjustment. It does NOT cover rate-limited conductance control or sensor-health fallback. P-01's mechanism is complementary, not overlapping — but the buyer's counsel should assess whether 'ML/AI adjustment of valve thresholds' could encompass P-01's rate limiting.

prior_art_landscape.title: Technical Considerations for Medical Devices with Physiologic Closed-Loop Control Technology
what_it_covers: FDA guidance for physiologic closed-loop controlled (PCLC) devices
prior_art_landscape.relevance_to_P-01: P-01 falls under FDA's PCLC guidance. Any buyer developing P-01 must follow this guidance for: (1) sensor validation, (2) control algorithm verification, (3) nonclinical testing, (4) animal model validation, (5) clinical trial design. This is a regulatory pathway, not a patent barrier — but it adds development cost and timeline.

prior_art_landscape.title: Telemetric intracranial pressure sensors with programmable valves
prior_art_landscape.relevance_to_P-01: Miethke's SENSOR RESERVOIR and similar products provide the HARDWARE that P-01 needs (sensor + valve). P-01 provides the CONTROL LAW. The hardware is not novel; the control law is the differentiator.

what_P-01_is_NOT_claiming: NOT claiming 'closed-loop shunt control' — US20210338992A1 covers this
NOT claiming 'sensor failure handling' — US20260115436A1 covers this
NOT claiming 'sensor-driven valve actuation' — multiple patents cover this
NOT claiming 'obstruction detection' — US20260115436A1 covers this
NOT claiming 'programmable valves' — decades of prior art
NOT claiming 'telemetric ICP sensing' — Miethke and others have this
what_P-01_IS_claiming: The specific combination of: bounded rate of conductance change (2%/sec) + sensor-health-aware safe fallback (freeze alpha) + continuous multi-segment redistribution (no hard isolation) + drainage floor + alpha floor
Demonstrated computational advantage: 2-3x over existing closed-loop approach across 9 attack modes
The robustness envelope this combination produces under realistic sensor uncertainty
buyer_question: Does bounded conductance-rate control produce a new robustness envelope under realistic sensor uncertainty, that is NOT already covered by US20260115436A1's sensor failure handling?
honest_assessment: The 2026 patent US20260115436A1 significantly narrows P-01's novelty. The sensor-health fallback concept is now in published prior art. P-01's remaining differentiation is the BOUNDED RATE mechanism (not just fallback) and the multi-segment continuous redistribution. These are narrow but potentially defensible. The buyer's IP counsel must make this determination.
